arxiv-2103-08058.title: On Planar Visibility Counting Problem
arxiv-2103-08058.creator: Sharareh Alipour
arxiv-2103-08058.description: Abstract For a set S S of n n disjoint line segments in ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} , the visibility counting problem is to preprocess S S such that the number of visible segments in S S from any query point p p can be computed quickly.

arxiv-2203-15459.title: Influence of Communication Among Shared Developers on the Productivity of Open Source Software Projects
arxiv-2203-15459.creator: Sairamvinay Vijayaraghavan, Jason (Jinxiao) Song, Terry Guan, Seongwoo Choi, Sutej Kulkarni
arxiv-2203-15459.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sairamvinay Vijayaraghavan, Jason (Jinxiao) Song, Terry Guan, Seongwoo Choi, Sutej Kulkarni. Many software developers rely on open source software for developing their applications and writing their source codes. Measuring an independent project’s overall productivity is still an open problem for many technology companies.

arxiv-2209-00213.title: Public Parking Spot Detection And Geo-localization Using Transfer Learning
arxiv-2209-00213.creator: Moseli Mots’oehli, Yao Chao Yang
arxiv-2209-00213.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Moseli Mots’oehli, Yao Chao Yang. In cities around the world, locating public parking lots with vacant parking spots is a major problem, costing commuters time and adding to traffic congestion. This work illustrates how a dataset of geo-tagged images from a mobile phone camera, can be used in navigating to the most convenient public parking lot in Johannesburg with an available parking space, detected by a neural network powered-public camera.

arxiv-2209-13266.title: Global fits of simplified models for dark matter with GAMBIT Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2209-13266.creator: Christopher Chang uq,a, Pat Scott qb, Tomás E. Gonzalo aachen,kitTTP, Felix Kahlhoefer aachen,kitTTP, Anders Kvellestad oslo, Martin White adelaide
arxiv-2209-13266.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christopher Chang uq,a, Pat Scott qb, Tomás E. Gonzalo aachen,kitTTP, Felix Kahlhoefer aachen,kitTTP, Anders Kvellestad oslo, Martin White adelaide. Simplified models provide a useful way to study the impacts of a small number of new particles on experimental observables and the interplay of those observables, without the need to construct an underlying theory. In this study, we perform global fits of simplified dark matter models with GAMBIT using an up-to-date set of likelihoods for indirect detection, direct detection and collider searches.

arxiv-2303-14783.title: A macroscopic constitutive relation for isotropic-genesis, polydomain liquid crystal elastomers Victoria Lee conducted this work while affiliated with the California Institute of Technology.
arxiv-2303-14783.creator: Victoria Lee, Adeline Wihardja, Kaushik Bhattacharya
arxiv-2303-14783.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Victoria Lee, Adeline Wihardja, Kaushik Bhattacharya. Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are rubber-like solids that incorporate nematic mesogens (stiff rod-like molecules) as a part of their polymer chains. In recent years, isotropic-genesis, polydomain liquid crystal elastomers (I-PLCEs) has been a topic of both scientific and technological interest due to their intriguing properties such as soft behavior, ability to dissipate energy and stimuli response, as well as the ease with which they can be synthesized.

arxiv-2307-02490.title: Unlocking the Resonant Structure of the New Poisson Equation
arxiv-2307-02490.creator: Mario J. Pinheiro
arxiv-2307-02490.description: Abstract This paper presents a modified form of the Poisson equation derived from a variational method. The equation can model resonant structures and various physical systems and can be solved using numerical techniques like finite element, boundary element, and spectral methods. Modifications to the Poisson equation can improve predictions and safety protocols.

arxiv-2312-07558.title: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints on f ⁡ ( T , 𝒯 ) f(T,\mathcal{T}) gravity
arxiv-2312-07558.creator: Sai Swagat Mishra, Ameya Kolhatkar, P.K. Sahoo
arxiv-2312-07558.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sai Swagat Mishra, Ameya Kolhatkar, P.K. Sahoo. Big Bang Nucleosynthesis provides us with an observational insight into the very early Universe. Since this mechanism of light element synthesis comes out of the standard model of particle cosmology which follows directly from General Relativity, it is expected that any modifications to GR will result in deviations in the predicted observable parameters which are mainly, the neutron-to-proton ratio and the baryon-to-photon ratio.

arxiv-2403-03090.title: Microelectronic readout of a diamond quantum sensor
arxiv-2403-03090.creator: D. Wirtitsch, G. Wachter, S. Reisenbauer, J. Schalko, U. Schmid, A. Fant, L. Sant, M. Trupke
arxiv-2403-03090.description: Abstract Quantum sensors based on the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond are rapidly advancing from scientific exploration towards the first generation of commercial applications. While significant progress has been made in developing suitable methods for the manipulation of the NV centre spin state, the detection of the defect luminescence has so far limited the performance of miniaturized sensor architectures.

arxiv-2406-00991.title: A High-Order Hybrid-Spectral Incompressible Navier-Stokes Model For Nonlinear Water Waves
arxiv-2406-00991.creator: Anders Melander, Max E. Bitsch, Dong Chen, Allan P. Engsig-Karup
arxiv-2406-00991.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anders Melander, Max E. Bitsch, Dong Chen, Allan P. Engsig-Karup. We present a new high-order accurate computational fluid dynamics model based on the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with a free surface for the accurate simulation of nonlinear and dispersive water waves in the time domain. The spatial discretization is based on Chebyshev polynomials in the vertical direction and a Fourier basis in the horizontal direction, allowing for the use of the fast Chebyshev and Fourier transforms for the efficient computation of spatial derivatives.

arxiv-2409-04710.title: Quantitative Estimates for the Size of the Zsigmondy Set in Arithmetic Dynamics
arxiv-2409-04710.description: Abstract Abstract Let K be a number field. We provide quantitative estimates for the size of the Zsigmondy set of an integral ideal sequence generated by iterating a polynomial function \varphi(z)\in K[z] at a wandering point \alpha\in K. Mathematics Subject Classification 2020. 11B83, 37P05, 11G50. Keywords. Primitive divisors, Divisibility sequence, Height function, Arithmetic dynamics. 1.

arxiv-2501-02133.title: Modified Condition/Decision Coverage in the GNU Compiler Collection
arxiv-2501-02133.creator: Jørgen Kvalsvik
arxiv-2501-02133.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jørgen Kvalsvik. We describe the implementation of the masking Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (MC/DC) support in GCC 14, a powerful structural coverage metric with wide industry adoption for safety critical applications. By analyzing the structure of Boolean expressions with Binary Decision Diagrams we can observe the key property of MC/DC, the power to independently affect the outcome, and map to the edges of the Control Flow Graph.

arxiv-2505-24582.title: The Dynamics of Infall and Accretion Shocks in the Outer Disk Facilities: ALMA
arxiv-2505-24582.creator: Susan Terebey, Loraine Sandoval Ascencio, Lizxandra Flores-Rivera, Neal J. Turner, Andrew Barajas
arxiv-2505-24582.description: Abstract High-spatial-resolution observations of disks around young stars suggest planetary systems begin forming early, during the protostellar phase ( ≤ \leq 1 Myr) when stars accrete most of their mass via infall from the surrounding cloud. During this era shocks are expected to be ubiquitous around the gaseous accretion disk due to supersonic infall that strikes the disk.

pmc-10738740.title: TARGETING HEALTH-PROMOTING ACTIVITY IN OLDER ADULTS WITH MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS AND FUNCTIONAL LIMITATIONS
pmc-10738740.creator: Tara Klinedinst, Nicholas Hollman, Carrie Ciro, Darla Kendzor
pmc-10738740.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Nearly half of older adults in the U.S. have multiple chronic health conditions in addition to functional limitations (MCC + FL) that restrict health self-management activities. We tested an innovative combination of occupational therapy (OT) and behavioral activation (BA) to improve health self-management using the goal setting, scheduling/monitoring activities, and problem-solving components of the BA approach, as well as skill building, environmental modification, activity adaptation, and focus on daily routines from OT (BA+OT).

pmc-12590009.title: Invasive mole after heterotopic pregnancy in a postmenopausal woman: A rare case report from a tertiary hospital in northern Tanzania
pmc-12590009.creator: John Lugata, Glory Maringo, Tecla Lyamuya, Eusebious Maro, Joseph Mlay, Alex Mremi
pmc-12590009.description: Introduction and importanceInvasive moles (IMs) are a rare form of gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) characterized by molar tissue made up of hydropic villi with an overgrowth of trophoblastic cells. These can penetrate the myometrium or uterine vessels in women of reproductive age. Its occurrence in postmenopausal women is exceedingly rare, and even more unusual when arising after a heterotopic pregnancy.

pmc-12747937.title: Identification of exosome miRNAs regulated by SPHK2 in human glioma cells
pmc-12747937.creator: Jing Liu, Huafu Zhao, Xia Liu, Xiaoyun Guan, Qiyu Guo, Yanwen Xu, Jinhua Qiu
pmc-12747937.description: BackgroundGlioma is the most common primary brain tumor, and the WHO 4 glioma, glioblastoma (GB), is a malignant tumor with high invasiveness and mortality. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), as the main immune cells in glioma, play an important role in the growth, invasiveness, immune escape, and drug resistance. The M2 phenotype of macrophages, but not the M1 phenotype, promotes glioma development.

pmc-12852798.title: A stationary phase-specific bacterial green light sensor for enhancing metabolite production
pmc-12852798.creator: John T Lazar, Daniel J Haller, Abbas Ghaddar, Jae J Kim, Kevin Yang, Sebastián M Castillo-Hair, Andrew R Gilmour, Ross Thyer, Jeffrey J Tabor
pmc-12852798.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Genetically-encoded sensors are used to control protein and metabolite production in bacterial fermentations. However, these sensors are generally optimized for exponential growth rather than stationary phase where production occurs. Here, we find that our previously engineered E. coli green light sensor CcaSR, which functions robustly in exponential phase, fails in stationary phase due to spontaneous loss of an engineered chromophore biosynthetic pathway and accumulation of CcaS and CcaR.

uslaw-usc-t29-s164.description: United States Code, Title 29 (Labor); Chapter 7 (Labor-Management Relations); Subchapter II (National Labor Relations). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Supervisors as union members Nothing herein shall prohibit any individual employed as a supervisor from becoming or remaining a member of a labor organization, but no employer subject to this subchapter shall be compelled to deem individuals defined herein as supervisors.
